title: The Month Bollywood Went to War With Itself — and Everyone Won
excerpt: Four Fridays, four different flavors of hit, and a combined gross north of ₹250 crore: June 2026 was the most competitive — and most rewarding — month in Hindi cinema history.
body:
June isn't just over. It's exhausted. And so is every multiplex manager from Juhu to Jersey City.

In a month that trade veteran **Taran Adarsh** warned would lead to "*maara-maari* for screens," Bollywood threw four consecutive Friday punches — each landing, each drawing blood, and each, improbably, finding its audience. The combined India net collections from June's Hindi releases are on track to cross **₹250 crore**, with two of the four tentpoles still very much in play. In an era where a single film's underperformance can send industry analysts into existential dread, June 2026 decided to flex.

<youtube>https://youtube.com/watch?v=-Iiv8Gq8WeY</youtube>


## The Dhawans Set the Table

It began, as Bollywood often does, with a father and a son. **Varun Dhawan** and director **David Dhawan** returned to the big screen together after nine years with *Hai Jawani Toh Ishq Hona Hai*, a romantic comedy that opened to ₹7.5 crore on June 5 and steadily built its way to a lifetime of approximately **₹50 crore net** in India and **₹71 crore worldwide**. Not a blockbuster. Not a disaster. But for a genre that everyone in the industry claims is "dead on arrival in the post-OTT world," it proved there's still a multiplex audience that will show up for a David Dhawan comedy — especially when you pair **Pooja Hegde** and **Mrunal Thakur** as the double leads. The film wrapped its run as Bollywood's **6th highest-grossing release of 2026**.

## The Sleeper That Wouldn't Sleep

Then came the month's most remarkable story. **Imtiaz Ali**'s *Main Vaapas Aaunga*, starring **Diljit Dosanjh**, **Naseeruddin Shah**, **Vedang Raina**, and **Sharvari**, opened on June 12 to a whisper — just **₹1.28 crore** on Day 1. The kind of number that usually means a film is done by Wednesday. Instead, it did the opposite. Word of mouth — fuelled by **A.R. Rahman**'s stunning score and a genuinely moving partition story — lifted it to ₹2.50 crore on Sunday. Then it held through the weekdays. Then the second weekend happened: **₹12.12 crore**, a **115% jump** over the first. Pinkvilla now projects a lifetime of **₹65-70 crore net**. Currently at ₹44.70 crore net in India and still running strong in its third weekend, it's the textbook definition of a sleeper hit.

For the diaspora, this was the one that hit closest to home — a film about return, belonging, and the borders we carry inside us.

## Shahid Kapoor's Redemption

If *Main Vaapas Aaunga* was the quiet earner, **Cocktail 2** was the one that announced itself. **Shahid Kapoor**, **Kriti Sanon**, and **Rashmika Mandanna** — directed by **Homi Adajania** — opened to ₹14.10 crore on June 19 and crossed **₹100 crore worldwide** within its first week. After nine days, it stands at **₹133.97 crore globally** with an India net of ₹83.06 crore, making it the **4th highest-grossing Bollywood film of 2026**. For Shahid, this is vindication after *O'Romeo*'s underperformance earlier this year. For the romantic comedy genre, it's a full-throated argument for survival.

## The Jungle Roars

And then, because June clearly hadn't had enough, **Akshay Kumar** walked into the room. *Welcome To The Jungle* — with an ensemble so stacked it practically needs its own census (**Suniel Shetty**, **Paresh Rawal**, **Arshad Warsi**, **Raveena Tandon**, **Lara Dutta**, **Jacqueline Fernandez**, **Disha Patani**, **Johnny Lever**, **Rajpal Yadav**) — collected **₹57.31 crore net** in its opening weekend, including a ₹3.93 crore paid preview. Worldwide gross: **₹75.63 crore** in four days. That's the **4th-biggest Bollywood opening weekend of 2026**, behind only *Dhurandhar 2* (₹466 crore), *Border 2* (₹129.89 crore), and *Bhooth Bangla* (₹65.65 crore).

## What This Means

When **Bollywood Hungama** wrote in early June that "₹1,400 crore+ are at stake," they weren't exaggerating — they were previewing. Between the Hindi releases, the still-climbing Imtiaz Ali film, and a comedy franchise that just posted the year's strongest opening for a non-action film, June proved that a crowded calendar doesn't automatically cannibalise business. It rewards quality, punishes mediocrity, and gives audiences a reason to go back to the theatre every single week.

Hollywood tried to compete: *Toy Story 5* crossed $300 million worldwide, while *Supergirl* stumbled with a $38 million opening. But in Indian multiplexes, the Hindi originals held their own.

The lesson is simple: give audiences four genuinely different films — a rom-com, a partition drama, a sequel with heat, and a legacy franchise — and they will show up. Four times.
